clue.text: Clothes collected, hopefully, from weaver and artist

parts.note: Nick Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
a drawer is someone who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: Garments gathered from a textile worker and a painter, with luck.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer is the British name for a hope chest: linen and clothes a young woman put by for married life, hence 'hopefully'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a store of household linen and garments saved up in anticipation of marriage, a trousseau.

clue.text: Such writing comes as a relief one feels

definitions.text: Such writing comes as a relief one feels

parts.words: Such writing comes as a relief one feels
parts.note: relief here is raised printing, not comfort: this script is read by touching its embossed dots

explanation.definitionFit: The tactile script for blind readers is made of raised dots felt with the fingertips.

clue.text: Chinese puzzle over butter's taste

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another sits above it in the grid

parts.note: tang is a sharp taste
a butter is something that butts, such as a ram

explanation.surface: A puzzle from China set beside the flavour of something that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Chinese dissection puzzle of seven flat shapes rearranged into figures.

clue.text: Mad don, perhaps, is a lone voice

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says take ODD MAN and work it out, giving the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A crazy university lecturer, say, stands as the single dissenter.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'perhaps' warns that the clue words are the result of the answer's own wordplay, with 'out' as an anagram signal applied to the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone who differs from all the rest, a solitary dissenting voice.

clue.text: Drive to find employment for Lebanese group

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in addresses
use means employment, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: A trip to look for work for a community in Lebanon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Druse (Druze) are a religious community found in Lebanon, Syria and Israel.

clue.text: Section of The Ring? Opera mounted in part of Greece

parts.note: an arc is a section of a ring or circle, not of Wagner's cycle

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means set going upwards, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: Aida is the Verdi opera

explanation.surface: Part of Wagner's Ring cycle, and an opera staged in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns AIDA into ADIA. 'The Ring' looks like Wagner's operas, but it is just a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is a region of the Peloponnese, a real Greek district as well as a pastoral ideal.

clue.text: Graceful poem is unfinished — one with six feet

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the poem word is dropped

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem
an ant, like every insect, has six legs

explanation.surface: A verse is left incomplete, written by someone with hexameter lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts ELEGY to ELEG. 'six feet' suggests a hexameter in metre, but it means six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant is a synonym for graceful, stylish and refined in movement or form.

clue.text: One puts out tongue in an offensive way

definitions.text: One puts out tongue in an offensive way

parts.words: One puts out tongue in an offensive way
parts.note: not a rude gesture: the tongue is a tongue of fire, and the offensive is a military attack

explanation.definitionFit: This weapon projects a jet of burning fuel, a fiery tongue, in attacks.

clue.text: Scholarly line brought profit

parts.note: earned means made money, brought in profit

explanation.surface: An academic line of work proved lucrative.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned is a synonym for scholarly, erudite and well read.

clue.text: Relative has a right to be doubtful

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: A family member is entitled to have doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclear means uncertain, open to doubt.

clue.text: Retired officers, cool and lean

parts.note: reserved means cool in manner, aloof
to list is to lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Ex-military men are aloof and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lean' looks like thin, but it is the verb: a listing ship leans to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: The reserved list was the roll of retired officers liable to be recalled to service.

clue.text: Feverish condition of adolescent love initially in girl

indicators.note: in tells us the opening letters go inside the girl's name

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A fever brought on by teenage romance in a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adolescent love' reads as teenage romance in the surface, but the two words only lend their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a disease spread by mosquitoes and marked by recurring fevers.

clue.text: Upright methods used on purpose

indicators.note: on places the methods word after the purpose word in this across clue

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
ways are methods

explanation.walkthrough: 'on purpose' reads as deliberately, but it is END with WAYS put on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Endways means with the end upwards, standing on end, upright.

clue.text: Some other method one measures heat by

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used in measuring gas supply.

clue.text: Elderly chap holds degree in fine art

indicators.note: holds means the elderly chap contains the degree

parts.note: an oldster is an old person
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: An old man holds a qualification in fine art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine art' stands for a painting by a great European painter of the past, the usual sense of the phrase in the art trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a great European painter before about 1800, or one of their paintings, a work of fine art.

clue.text: Revolutionary government guide

definitions.meaning: the ... ruled France in 1795-99 during the Revolution
a book listing names and addresses, as a guide to finding people

explanation.definitionFit: The French five-man executive was so called, and the word also names a reference listing.

clue.text: The thinking man's telescope?

parts.note: a play on the phrase the thinking man's: a man who thinks is one kind of instrument, and one telescope design uses a mirror

explanation.definitionFit: A person given to reflection is one, and a telescope using a mirror rather than lenses is one too.

clue.text: Emotional thrill for loving and giving boy?

parts.note: from the nursery rhyme line Friday's child is loving and giving, so this is Fri's, Friday's
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Excitement for a boy who is affectionate and generous.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme Monday's Child, well known in Britain, says Friday's child is loving and giving; so the boy is Fri's son.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden shiver of excitement or emotion.

clue.text: Hurt look?

parts.note: not a pained expression but a gaze believed to do harm

explanation.definitionFit: This is the malevolent stare superstition says can bring misfortune.

clue.text: One who joins up to go peacefully with the troops?

definitions.text: One who joins up to go peacefully with the troops?

parts.words: One who joins up to go peacefully with the troops?
parts.note: he enlists but carries no weapon, and he also joins couples in marriage

explanation.definitionFit: An army chaplain serves with the forces as a non-combatant.

clue.text: The hat one might have to eat!

definitions.text: The hat one might have to eat!

parts.words: The hat one might have to eat!
parts.note: plays on the saying I'll eat my hat: this style of hat shares its name with a meat pastry

explanation.walkthrough: The style is a low round felt hat; the pastry is a British savoury of pork in hot-water crust.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-crowned felt hat is named after the British pastry filled with chopped pig meat.

clue.text: Face shock treatment for nonstandard speech

parts.note: dial is slang for face
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: Treating a face with electric shocks to fix the way someone talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional variety of a language differing from the standard form.

clue.text: Swimmer injured in the side

indicators.note: in tells us the injured word sits inside the side word

parts.note: a wing is a side, of a building or a team
hit means struck, injured

explanation.surface: A swimmer is hurt in the flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' means a fish, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The whiting is a sea fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Increase strength of outfit

definitions.meaning: as when a wind is said to ..., rising in force
a set of clothes, often unusual

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means rise in force, and as a noun it is an outfit or costume.

clue.text: Prematurely conclude dog has something to wag

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a tail is what a dog wags

explanation.surface: A mutt has a tail to wave about.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut short, ending something early.

clue.text: Regard relation

definitions.meaning: as in the phrase with ... to, meaning in relation to

explanation.definitionFit: The word means esteem, and also a point of reference or connection.

clue.text: Stamp on work papers

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: Put a mark on a work's documents.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to crush or subdue, to trample people down.

clue.text: One won't quite settle up — amend entry when worked out

indicators.note: worked out means the letters are reorganised into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone avoids paying in full and must correct the ledger once the sums are done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges UP and AMEND ENTRY together. 'One' is not a person: it is a payment that does not fully clear a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying less than is owed leaves a bill only partly cleared.
